definition: OpenAI's models - GPT, the reasoning models, embeddings, image and audio - hosted in Azure under Azure's terms: prompts and outputs are not used for training or shared with OpenAI, access is through Entra ID or keys, private endpoints and Azure Policy apply, and you choose where requests are processed. The API matches OpenAI's, so the official SDKs work. It is one family within Foundry Models.
example: The shop's assistant calls an Azure OpenAI deployment in Sweden Central with a managed identity; key access is disabled.

definition: The model catalogue in Microsoft Foundry: Azure OpenAI's models, models sold directly by Azure such as Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek, Grok and Phi, and partner and open models. Most deploy as pay-per-token endpoints hosted by Microsoft; some can be deployed to managed compute billed by the hour. Pick the provider for its contract, then the model for the task.
example: The team compares a small OpenAI model and Phi on the same 200 descriptions before choosing one.

definition: The unit a language model reads and writes - a piece of a word, roughly four characters or three-quarters of an English word. Models are priced per million input and output tokens, with output several times dearer, and limits such as context windows and quotas are counted in tokens.
example: A product prompt of 800 tokens and a 250-token description, times 40,000 products, is the whole cost estimate.

definition: The maximum number of tokens a model can take in and produce in one call - everything it can 'see' at once: system prompt, conversation history, retrieved documents and the answer. Windows range from about 128,000 tokens to over a million, but every token is paid for on every call, and material in the middle of long prompts gets less attention.
example: The assistant keeps the last ten turns plus a summary, instead of resending an hour-long conversation.

definition: The first message in a request to a chat model, setting its role, rules, tone and output format for the rest of the conversation. Most quality gains come from improving it - clear instructions, a few examples, a required JSON schema - before any retrieval or fine-tuning. Keep it in source control and evaluate changes like code.
example: "You write product descriptions for Northline. 80-120 words, British English, never invent materials, return JSON with title and body."

definition: A named instance of one model version in a Foundry or Azure OpenAI resource, which is what applications actually call. Its deployment type sets where requests are processed (globally, within an EU or US data zone, or in one region) and how you pay (per token, half-price batch, or provisioned units); its capacity is a share of the subscription's quota.
example: desc-batch is a small model on Global Batch; assistant is the same model on Data Zone Standard, because customers type personal data into it.

definition: The capacity unit for pay-per-token model deployments. Each subscription has a TPM quota per model, region and deployment type, shared out among its deployments; requests per minute are derived from it. Exceeding it returns 429 with a retry-after header, so clients must back off and retry.
example: Dev's script died at 2,000 products because its deployment had 10,000 TPM and no retry logic.

definition: Reserved model-processing capacity for a deployment, billed per unit per hour or through monthly and yearly reservations, whether used or not. It gives predictable latency and throughput for steady, heavy traffic; bursts above it can spill over to a pay-per-token deployment.
example: Once the assistant's traffic is steady, a small PTU reservation covers the daytime baseline and evening peaks spill to Data Zone Standard.

definition: Further training a model on your own examples so it adopts a style, format or narrow skill - often letting a small model match a large one on one task. It is poor at teaching facts, which go stale; improve the prompt and add retrieval first. Fine-tuned deployments carry an hourly hosting charge.
example: After 500 approved descriptions, a small model is fine-tuned to write in the house style without a long system prompt.
